units.name: Introduction
units.assessment: Before any drug is stopped, what four things must you establish for a patient facing a procedure — the bleeding risk of the operation, the patient's thrombotic risk, which antithrombotic they are taking, and how urgent the surgery is — and who on the care team owns each of those decisions?

lesson.title: Perioperative Management of Anticoagulants: What clinicians need to know in 2021
lesson.why: A single sitting that frames the whole perioperative problem — who is on which drug, what the procedure risks, and how the stop/restart decision is built — which is exactly the orientation this introductory section provides.

drills.name: Anticoagulation in the hard cases
drills.title: Special Populations and Anticoagulation with Dr Jim Douketis

units.name: Perioperative challenges and the importance of communication
units.assessment: When the bleeding risk and the thrombotic risk are both judged high, what specific conversation do you need to have with the proceduralist and with whoever prescribes the anticoagulant, and what must the written plan hand over to the patient, the pharmacist and the ward team?

lesson.title: Implementation of Anticoagulation Stewardship Programs: The Future of Anticoagulation Care
lesson.why: Anticoagulation stewardship is the systems answer to this section's point that periprocedural harm usually comes from handoffs rather than from the drugs themselves.

drills.name: Who owns the DOAC plan
drills.title: The role of the pharmacist in Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) management 2020

units.name: Perioperative venous thromboembolism prevention
units.assessment: Which surgical populations warrant pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis rather than mechanical measures alone, how does a risk-assessment model feed that decision, and what do patients undergoing major orthopedic surgery typically receive and for how long?

lesson.title: VTE Prevention-an update
lesson.why: A dedicated update on surgical thromboprophylaxis — risk assessment models, who gets pharmacologic prophylaxis, and duration — which is the whole content of this section.

drills.name: Perioperative case walkthrough
drills.title: Perioperative Management with Dr Eric Tseng

units.name: Perioperative anticoagulation management
units.assessment: How many days before surgery do you stop a DOAC compared with a vitamin K antagonist, which patients on warfarin genuinely benefit from short-acting bridging, and how does the bleeding risk of the procedure change when you restart afterwards?

lesson.title: Perioperative Management of Anticoagulation: Can You Clear My Patient for a Procedure?
lesson.why: Built around the exact consult question this section answers — clearing a patient for a procedure — with explicit interruption intervals and the shrinking indications for bridging.

units.name: Antiplatelet management
units.assessment: Which antiplatelet agents are held before surgery and for how long — aspirin, clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor — and how does a recent coronary stent change whether the procedure should be delayed rather than the drug interrupted?

lesson.title: New CHEST Guideline: Perioperative Management of Antithrombotic Therapy
lesson.why: The CHEST perioperative antithrombotic guideline session that gives the agent-by-agent hold intervals for antiplatelets and the rule that aspirin usually continues.

units.name: Intraoperative and postoperative bleeding management considerations
units.assessment: For life-threatening bleeding, which reversal strategy matches which drug — idarucizumab, andexanet alfa, four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate, intravenous vitamin K — and what should your institution already have protocolized before that call comes in?

lesson.title: Bleeding management and resuming anticoagulation workshop with Dr D Siegal
lesson.why: A workshop devoted to managing anticoagulant-associated bleeding and deciding when to resume, which is the double question this section poses.

units.name: Conclusion
units.assessment: Can you talk an entire periprocedural plan through out loud — stop date, bridging decision, day-of-surgery instruction, restart timing and the bleeding contingency — for a patient on apixaban for atrial fibrillation who is booked for colonoscopy with polypectomy?

lesson.title: Management of Perioperative Anticoagulation – Please participate in our 3-minute survey below!
lesson.why: A compact single-talk synthesis of the whole perioperative algorithm, useful as the consolidating pass this concluding section calls for.
